title: a satisfies, a satisfies followed by a cast, a const that holds one, and a double alias all leave a foreign constructor, property read and tag foreign, and every one is refused at the same rule as the direct spelling
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary': 'Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked panic case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration. Trusted @throws {never} metadata opts out.' The opt-out is a property of the DECLARATION the checker resolves, and `satisfies` resolves to the same declaration it started from — it checks an expression against a type and returns the expression's own type unchanged. So none of the wrappers here can make a foreign value less foreign, and the refusal must be the same one the direct spelling gets. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: on 2026-08-27 a lane closed 227 `satisfies` divergences between the two backends while conformance reported 0 divergent throughout, because no corpus case put a `satisfies` anywhere near a foreign value. `satisfies` is the shape most likely to be mistaken for a cast by a rule that strips type-only syntax, and a rule that strips it in the WRONG direction — treating the wrapped expression as a fresh, marker-free one — over-refuses, while one that strips it and loses the provenance under-refuses. Both failure modes existed. THE ROW THAT MAKES THIS CASE OBSERVE ANYTHING is `propVsALocal` at line 20: the alternate in the `??` is a LOCAL object, not another foreign one. With a foreign alternate the diagnostic fires whichever branch the rule looked at, and the case would be green while observing nothing — which is the vacuity this line exists to prevent. `propComma` at line 21 is the same idea on the comma operator, where the DISCARDED operand is the local one. THE DIRECT SPELLINGS ARE DECLARED ALONGSIDE the wrapped ones on purpose (lines 10, 15 and 23): without them the case cannot distinguish 'the wrapper preserved the provenance' from 'this whole file is refused for some unrelated reason', and with them the promise is an equality between spellings rather than a list of refusals. WHAT THIS CASE PINS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT: it pins three rules at seventeen authored positions, as a sorted multiset — the two backends emit them in different orders and the judge compares sets. It does NOT declare `messageContains` anywhere. `SMITHERS1504` and `SMITHERS1506` carry a fixed remediation sentence with no payload naming this program, and the two backends word `SMITHERS1506` completely differently ('expression-safe Result lowering is deferred' versus 'need an annotated adapter before they can enter checked code'), so any fragment common to both would be a name for the rule, which is the use the corpus README's worked counter-example forbids. The `SMITHERS1101`s on lines 23-25 are declared IN FULL rather than filtered: the tagged-template functions carry an explicit `: string` return, so the panic case they acquire cannot be represented, and 'which diagnostics fire' is part of the contract. The constructor and property functions deliberately have NO explicit return type, because with one the two backends disagree about `SMITHERS1101` — a recorded residual — and this case is written to be identical on both without an `xfail`. It also deliberately does not RETURN the constructed foreign value: doing so adds a `SMITHERS1508` per constructor row, which is a different rule about escaping provenance and would make this case's failures harder to read. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column on line 20 — the `propVsALocal` row, the load-bearing one — from 34 to 31 (the column its comma sibling reports, so the mutation is a plausible answer rather than a nonsense one) turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 96e9e8830ce7b32d29db50941b61200d0e6b02b17d228e6feba626ada0c1c128 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired positive controls are `an-ordinary-satisfies-a-cast-and-an-annotation-stay-clean`, where the same three wrappers around LOCAL values and TRUSTED foreign ones must compile and RUN, and `an-as-or-an-annotation-erases-a-trust-marker-where-satisfies-does-not`, which holds the boundary from the other side.
